reaction: The location requirement was consistent with the packaging step.

reason: Glucose is already in villus blood; inspecting it may reveal the next available connection.

effect: Inspecting glucose revealed its sole partner and automatically combined both nutrients into portal blood, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The automatic combination resolved the route, though I had expected a vessel or location to be involved.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following fat from intestinal cells into chylomicrons and then lymph made its route distinct from glucose and amino acids; the descriptions also explain that intestinal cells rebuild and package fat.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the villus after the fat route was complete returned no partners, so it did not directly advance the remaining goal.

surprise.text: Fat packaging and lacteal entry each required the villus hotspot rather than a direct combination with the named material; compatibility feedback completed both operations automatically.

arbitrary.text: Combining the two nutrients already in villus blood to represent their shared portal route felt less physically intuitive than connecting them to a vessel, although the resulting description explains their destination.

continue.text: I would continue to see how absorbed nutrients are used after reaching the liver and blood. The contrasting routes were informative, though the location-dependent commands took some trial and feedback.
